one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-04 holds no Oracle earnings (Q2 FY27 is ~mid-December). Scheduled: Oracle AI World, Las Vegas Oct 25-28 (management said gross-margin detail on the AI infrastructure ramp would come at an October event; that could cut either way); Big-4 hyperscaler Q3 reports in the last week of October, which per our standing capex file bring the first numeric 2027 capex guides (2026 guides were only ever raised, so a supportive read-through for AI-infra names is more likely than not); FOMC late October. OpenAI funding/IPO headlines are an unscheduled two-way risk (Polymarket prices >=$1.25T valuation by year-end at 84%, i.e. funding is not seen as stressed). Post-earnings drift from the Sept 10 beat is largely played out. I stay close to a symmetric lognormal around spot with a slight +0.8% tilt for the event read-through, sigma 16.5% for the month (56% annual vol / 3.5, nudged up for event density).

fair_value.method: Blend of 12-month-forward P/E (NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct-2027 of ~$12.97 consensus haircut 15% to $11.0 x 15x = $165, weight 0.6) and EV/EBITDA (NTM EBITDA ~$88B haircut 15% to $75B x 9x less ~$150B net debt over ~3.15B shares = $167, weight 0.4).

FY28 EPS needs revenue +46% (MarketScreener $131.7B) on a single-customer-heavy backlog; 2-year-out consensus for capex-heavy names has a pro-cyclical revision history (capex file, Meta 2023) and OpenAI has missed internal targets; ATM dilution ($20B in Q1) and rising interest cost also hit per-share EPS.

Inside peer range 10.5-27.0x, below the 21.5x median; Oracle's own 10-yr TTM P/E min 14.4x. Discount justified by negative FCF through FY28, net debt rising to ~$147B, top-customer concentration (OpenAI $300B contract) and non-GAAP excluding SBC/amortization (~18% gap) whereas MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL/META report near-GAAP.

bear.story: AI capex digestion or OpenAI renegotiates/defers part of its ~$300B commitment; 2027 recession (Kalshi 23%, Polymarket 34%) hits financing; FY28 EPS revised to ~$8-9 and stock trades ~10x with credit-spread stress and more equity issuance.

base.story: OCI grows >70%, FY27 hits >=$90B revenue, FY28 EPS lands ~10-15% below today's consensus, FCF still negative but customer prepayments/BYO-hardware cap net capex at ~$70B; multiple ~15x NTM non-GAAP.

bull.story: RPO converts on schedule, AI-infra gross margins flatten as guided, FY29 FCF turns positive visibly, OpenAI raises at >=$1.25T and IPO path clears; re-rate toward peer median ~20x on ~$12.5 NTM EPS (like META's 2023 recovery after a 2022 capex scare).

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount to median persists through the horizon because (1) FCF is negative through FY28 per consensus (-$37B FY27, -$33B FY28) while every big-cloud peer funds capex from FCF; (2) net debt rises to ~$147B and equity is being issued via ATM; (3) RPO is concentrated in one counterparty (OpenAI) that has missed internal targets; (4) Oracle's non-GAAP EPS excludes SBC and amortization, inflating it ~18% vs the near-GAAP figures of MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL/META. Not a deeper discount because OCI growth (+121%) and RPO ($664B) give it the highest revenue growth in the set.

reasoning: Anchor: ORCL is down ~51% in a year with 56% realized vol, after a 2024-25 re-rating to a >30x multiple on the OpenAI-driven RPO. Base rates: the Counterpoint drawdown study shows stocks that suffered ~50-60% drawdowns had high median 1-year returns, but that is measured from the trough and >half of stocks never regain prior highs, so I use it only as a mild offset to 12-month loser momentum (Jegadeesh-Titman style continuation), netting to a roughly neutral-to-slightly-positive drift. Analogs: META 2022-23 (capex scare, -76% then +194% once FCF stayed positive) vs telecom-capex busts of 2001 (vendor/financing-dependent builders kept falling). Oracle sits between: unlike META, it has negative FCF and rising leverage; unlike 2001 carriers, revenue is contracted ($664B RPO, OCI +121%, Q1 beat on Sept 10, FY27 guide >=$90B, non-GAAP EPS $8.10). Valuation: at $143 it trades 14.5x CY27 non-GAAP (17.7x GAAP-ish) vs an 11-peer median of 21.5x on a consistent calendar-2027 basis, and ~8.7x CY27 EBITDA; my blended 12-month fair value is $165 after a 15% haircut to 2-years-out consensus. Prediction markets show OpenAI funding not under acute stress (84% >= $1.25T valuation by year-end, $1.26M volume) but 2027 recession odds of 23-34% fatten the left tail. Scenarios 30% $90 / 45% $160 / 25% $245 give a mean ~$160 and median ~$150; the ladder blends that 3-component lognormal mixture with a single lognormal (median $150, sigma 0.50), putting P(>=spot) at 0.56. Research note: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and Twelve Data estimates gated, so consensus came from the Nasdaq/Zacks feed, StockAnalysis and MarketScreener; peer EV/EBITDA is TTM not forward; CRM and WDAY CY27 non-GAAP EPS (18.0, 13.6) are my extrapolations from next-FY street EPS.
